sessionId.locator: thread.started.thread_id, first row of the public JSONL event stream the runner captures from the client

providers.notes: The only vendor with a capture reader, so the only one the derivation stamps runner_enforced. The session id is announced rather than pinned, so the rollout must be searched for under the sessions root and matched to the public thread.started id — codex-rollout.mjs does that walk and rejects anything outside the root. Strongest at driving the dev loop as well. Historical strict-code-mode and direct-MCP receipts remain readable through src/blind/receipt_binding.ts.

sessionId.locator: --session-id <uuid>, appended by the runner at launch. It is NOT in launch.argv because PlaytestLaunchSchema substitutes only {MODEL}, {CWD} and {MCP_CONFIG}; a {SESSION_ID} token would let the flag live here, and until one exists the runner must append the pair itself.

providers.notes: The second vendor the derivation stamps runner_enforced, and the one that proves the seam is a seam rather than a Codex-shaped hole. Stronger to capture than codex: --session-id PINS the id, so the log path is exact BEFORE launch and the reader never has to pick the newest file in a directory and hope no other Claude Code was running. No rootEnv is declared — CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR exists, but this checkout has not verified that it relocates the per-session log, and naming an env var on faith is exactly the lie this file exists to prevent; the pinned id already keeps concurrent cohort members apart under one shared root. The old argv here was decorative and wrong in two ways: --permission-mode plan REFUSES the game's state-mutating tools, so every session would have died on the first step_action, and --add-dir {CWD} handed the player filesystem access it must never have. The replacement is the flag set verified live against claude 2.1.251: --tools "" removes every built-in tool, --strict-mcp-config plus --mcp-config admits only the adventureforge server, --setting-sources "" and --disable-slash-commands drop settings, skills and hooks, and the init event on the stream reports the resulting surface back so blind-tester/claude-session.mjs can audit what was OFFERED, not merely what was called.

Well suited to cheap mass-parallel volume cohorts. Ships a CLI, but declares no capture block — nothing here can locate or read its session logs — so the registry DERIVES operator_attested and its sessions are hand-played and ingested until a reader module exists.

kind=desktop_client, so the derivation can never reach runner_enforced for this entry no matter what else is written here. A headless-capable Grok CLI DOES ship now (verified: grok 1.0.5 offers -p/--single, --output-format, --tools and an mcp subcommand), so the old 'no CLI exists' note was stale. This stays operator_attested and kind=desktop_client anyway, deliberately: `blind-tester/run.sh` can only PROVE blindness for codex, by reading Codex's own rollout logs, and flipping this to headless_cli would let a grok cohort past argument validation only to die inside the runner. Grok also takes its prompt as an argument rather than on STDIN, and has no --mcp-config flag, so it does not fit the launch contract either. Sessions are captured in the client and ingested with `npm run playtest:ingest`; revisit only when a rollout-log reader for this vendor exists.
